title: Priming SNR microbench journal — scratch
content:
Overview:
- Quick personal scratchpad investigating how different priming strategies (prefix tokens + cached KV) change the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of latency measurements for short completion requests (<=128 output tokens).
- Trying to characterize when priming noise dominates tail p95/p99 variance vs. when system jitter is the limiter.
- Testbed: single dedicated GPU on dev cluster (a2-large-ish sim), model: rw-1b-qat (4-bit quantized), runtime: local dev binary (build 2025-09-10).

Hypothesis:
- Adding a short semantic primer (10-50 tokens of context) increases median latency by X ms but improves output quality; however it increases variance in p99 due to cache pressure and KV assembly cost.
- Synthetic noise primers (random tokens) should increase warmup cost but not quality; useful to separate pure runtime priming cost from semantic priming cost.

Experiment config (kept intentionally minimal):
- Ingress pattern: steady poisson arrivals at target QPS (2.5 qps, 5 qps, 10 qps) for 10m runs.
- Request payloads: 16B prompt (base) + primer (0/10/30/60 tokens)
notes:
- concurrency per worker pinned to 8.
  - batching disabled for first pass to see raw per-request latency.
  - measured: median, p95, p99, stddev, sample_count, mean_tokens_per_request.
raw_runs:
CSV-style lines (cmd output snippet):
run_id,primer_type,primer_len,qps,median_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,stddev_ms,sample_count
r1,none,0,2.5,42,78,126,9.2,1500
r2,semantic,10,2.5,56,110,210,24.6,1500
r3,semantic,30,2.5,68,138,320,48.3,1500
r4,random,30,2.5,65,130,295,44.8,1500
r5,none,10,5,44,82,140,11.1,3000
r6,semantic,10,5,62,132,260,30.5,3000
r7,semantic,60,10,89,260,680,130.4,6000
r8,random,60,10,85,240,610,118.9,6000

Interpretation notes:
- Median increases roughly linearly with primer length (~0.6-0.8 ms/token) for this model/runtime when batching is off.
- p99 balloons superlinearly with long semantic primers under higher QPS: suggests KV cache assembly + memory churn is non-linear (possibly O(n) per primer token with heavy traffic).
- Random primers produce similar median cost but slightly lower p99 than semantic primers at same length -> indicates that semantic tokens likely cause additional compute (attention density?) or at least produce more variable internal states (cache misses?).

SNR heuristic attempt (informal):
- Define measurement SNR = median_ms / stddev_ms. Higher is better (cleaner signal).
- r1 SNR = 42 / 9.2 = 4.6 (clean)
- r3 SNR = 68 / 48.3 = 1.4 (noisy)
- r7 SNR = 89 / 130.4 = 0.68 (dominated by noise)

Quick ASCII micro-plot (median vs primer_len at 5 qps):
median_ms | primer_len
   70    | 0  -> 44ms
  110    | 10 -> 62ms
  145    | 30 -> 76ms (interpolated)
  180    | 60 -> 89ms

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a run with batching enabled (batch size 8, adaptive) to see whether batching amortizes priming cost or amplifies p99.
- Investigate memory profiler during semantic primer runs: is there a transient allocation spike during KV construction? (compare RSS and GPU memory timeline).
- Try pre-populating KV cache via synthetic warm traffic before a long primer to see if p99 improves (cache priming).
- Re-run on rw-3b-quant and rw-350m to compare scale effects: is per-token cost linear across sizes?
- Add an experiment with prefix compression (send primer hashed tokens that expand server-side) to measure the overhead of parsing vs attention compute.

Quick conclusions (for stand-up):
- Short primers (<=10 tokens) are reasonable at low QPS.
- Long semantic primers (>30 tokens) drastically increase tail latency variability at moderate-to-high QPS — likely unacceptable for low-latency endpoints if batching disabled.
- Random primers cause similar median cost but slightly less tail risk; suggests part of tail is model-state-dependent rather than purely length-dependent.

Immediate next actions:
- Run 3 repeat runs with batching=8 at 5 qps for primer_len in [0,10,30,60] and collect p95/p99. (assign to Liam P.)
- Add lightweight mem-trace (GPU + host) during r3-r7 style runs (assign to Mira S.).
- Draft short note for product: include tradeoffs on recommending primer length for low-latency endpoints.

Random scribbles / ideas:
- Could try a hybrid: store last-KV snapshots for common primers and apply quick merge on request (too complex?).
- Use primer fingerprinting to route long-primer requests to a separate warm pool (routing policy idea).

End of scratchpad — will iterate after batching+mem runs.
